common: Read the approved `AGENTS.md`, `docs/implementation-plan.md`, and `docs/website-spec.md` before coding. The plan owns behavior; the website spec and `docs/website-reference.html` own presentation. For material design changes, update the specification and reference together. UI handoffs include actual desktop/phone screenshots and relevant states. Fixture data is not a production default.

issues.title: Confirm household CSV profiles, currency, attribution, and deployment
issues.goal: Record the household inputs needed to finish import support and deployment without expanding MVP scope.
criteria: Document the first required CSV exports: headers, date/amount conventions, source transaction ID availability, and account types. Use anonymized fixtures; keep real statements out of the public repository.
Record the initial sheet currency and attribution labels. Ethan, Parents, and USD in the visual reference remain demo values unless confirmed.
Record private-network versus HTTPS access and the intended host/backup location.
Link decisions and fixture locations from the implementation plan. Foundation work can proceed before these decisions; supported-profile and release checks cannot.

issues.title: Scaffold Next.js, Drizzle SQLite, Docker, and development checks
issues.goal: Create the runnable application foundation specified by the plan.
criteria: Set up Next.js App Router with TypeScript and a standalone Docker build; add reproducible development, build, lint, type-check, and test commands.
Configure Drizzle migrations and SQLite with foreign keys, appropriate WAL/busy handling, and a persistent /data volume. Run one application process; do not add a separate scheduler service.
Use a separate /backups mount and documented environment configuration. Keep credentials and database files out of source control.
Add CI for the applicable build/type/lint checks and focused tests. A fresh Docker instance starts, applies migrations safely, and retains a persisted test record across restart.
Keep application scaffolding free of production demo accounts and fixture transactions.

issues.title: Implement authentication, first-admin setup, and controlled registration
issues.goal: Let each family member sign in independently and let the host control account creation.
criteria: Integrate Better Auth's Drizzle schema and username plugin. Registration requires email, username, display name, and password; sign-in accepts the documented email/username flow.
Protect first-admin creation with the configured setup token and an atomic first-admin check. Concurrent setup requests cannot create multiple initial admins; disable setup after completion.
Honor controlled-registration configuration and build the specified setup/sign-in/registration states with accessible validation and session expiry handling.
Provide the documented host CLI password-recovery path and invalidate affected sessions. Do not show an email-reset flow without an implemented email delivery service.
Verify unauthorized requests and setup/registration races. Administrator status does not grant sheet membership or financial access.
Match the website spec's auth presentation; integrate shared components from the app-shell issue when available.

issues.title: Implement sheet creation, ownership, and server-side access checks
issues.goal: Create the security boundary for all financial reads and writes.
criteria: Create sheets with one currency and owner_id as the ownership authority; sheet_members contains accepted non-owner members only.
Create protected Uncategorized and Unassigned defaults atomically with a sheet. Reject partial sheet creation.
Apply a central server-side access check on every sheet-scoped operation; validate that referenced accounts, categories, buckets, and transactions belong to the same sheet.
Build sheet creation, selection, and the no-sheet welcome state. Remember selection only while access remains valid.
Verify unrelated users cannot read/write using guessed IDs, and administrators have no financial access solely through the admin role.
Leave membership transitions to the sharing issue, using the same authorization boundary.

issues.title: Implement validated SQLite snapshots and offline restore commands
issues.goal: Provide a safe recovery path before storing household data.
criteria: Create consistent snapshots using the SQLite backup API or VACUUM INTO; never copy only the live database file while WAL writes may be present.
Validate snapshot integrity and schema/application compatibility. Write snapshots atomically to /backups; retain required metadata.
Implement host export and offline restore commands. Restore requires a stopped app, a validated backup, preservation of the existing database, and removal/replacement of stale WAL sidecars.
Require fresh sign-in after restore while recovering users and memberships. Clearly document the whole-database scope and sensitivity of host backups.
Run a fresh-volume restore drill for available schema entities and reject a corrupted or incompatible snapshot without damaging the existing database.
Leave scheduling, retention, and admin status to the backup-operations issue; leave browser download/restore outside MVP.

issues.title: Build shared design tokens, components, and responsive application shell
issues.goal: Give every subsequent screen the same Homebooks visual language and navigation.
criteria: Implement the exact website-spec color, typography, spacing, radius, and focus tokens in one shared source. Use system sans and tabular numerals for amounts.
Build shared buttons, labeled fields, selectors, dialogs/drawers, tables/cards, badges, budget bars, notices, and loading/empty/error states.
Implement desktop/tablet sidebar, phone navigation drawer, top bar, sheet switcher, and month selector at the specified breakpoints. Show the current sheet and month clearly.
Provide a global invitation entry point, including when the user has no sheets; wire it when invitation data is available.
Verify 1440px and 390px appearance against the reference, keyboard focus and dialog behavior, 44px touch targets, and no page overflow at 320px.
Use the reference for appearance only. Actual navigation and actions must operate on application data; no decorative charts or fixture production defaults.

issues.title: Implement financial accounts, categories, and attribution settings
issues.goal: Let authorized sheet users organize expenses without destroying historical records.
criteria: Implement the plan's account/category/bucket schema, validation, and sheet-scoped create/rename/archive operations.
Keep Uncategorized and Unassigned protected. Archive referenced entities instead of deleting history; exclude archived entities from new selections while displaying them on existing records.
Build Settings sections and dialogs for sheet information, accounts, categories, attribution, and profile using the website spec.
Enforce owner-only operations where specified; members may perform the permitted financial organization work. Do not implement owner transfer.
Verify archived/history behavior, cross-sheet reference rejection, duplicate/name validation, empty states, and failed saves.
Make at least one active financial account available before transaction entry or guide the user to create one.

issues.title: Implement transaction and split rules with atomic writes and edit conflicts
issues.goal: Store manual and imported transactions with reliable money and attribution rules.
criteria: Store integer minor units and date-only transaction dates. Expenses are negative, refunds positive; income and transfer records are excluded from spending.

Require at least one split with category and attribution bucket from the same sheet. Split amounts have the transaction sign, contain no zero or mixed-sign rows, and sum exactly to the transaction amount.
Create/update transaction and splits atomically. Use version checks to reject stale edits rather than overwriting another person's changes.
Implement tombstone deletion and preserve immutable import identity after edits or deletion. Exclude deleted transactions from reports.
Provide one shared spending calculation for category, attribution, and month reporting; negate expense/refund splits. Credit-card payments remain transfers even when both sides are recorded.
Verify the $100 expense split $60/$40, $20 refund, income exclusion, transfer exclusion, cross-sheet references, invalid split sums, and concurrent edits with literal expected amounts.

issues.title: Build transaction ledger, filters, and split entry drawer
issues.goal: Let family members review spending and enter or correct transactions on desktop and phone.
criteria: Implement the specified desktop columns and phone cards, sheet/month context, filters, and 50-row pagination.
Build the 520px desktop entry drawer and phone fullscreen form with account, local date, payee, kind, positive magnitude, category, and attribution. Transfer direction determines the stored sign.
Support split editing and show the exact total/remaining-to-allocate amount. Default category/bucket to the protected values; guide account creation when no active account exists.
Preserve unsaved input on validation, network, and stale-version errors; show a reviewable conflict before retrying. Prevent accidental double submissions.
Implement confirmation and tombstone delete behavior, loading/empty/no-match states, permission loss, and accessible focus return.
Check actual manual entry, refund, transfer, split, edit, and delete flows; include desktop and phone screenshots in the handoff.

issues.title: Implement CSV mapping, normalization, and validation previews
issues.goal: Turn supported statement exports into reviewable normalized rows without writing transactions yet.
criteria: Implement bounded CSV upload/parsing with documented file and row limits, encoding/header handling, and account selection scoped to the sheet.
Support the plan's mapping/profile fields including date, payee, signed amount or debit/credit columns, and optional source ID. Let users select date/amount conventions explicitly.
Normalize money to integer minor units and dates to date-only values; do not guess ambiguous dates or silently round malformed values.
Return per-row validation errors and preview data; require correction or explicit exclusion of invalid rows before confirmation.
Version mapping/profile configuration and bind the preview to file, account, mapping, and caller context. Preview performs no financial writes.
Verify parsing with anonymized fixtures and edge cases; the final household-specific profiles depend on the household-input issue.

issues.title: Implement import identity, duplicate review, and idempotent atomic commit
issues.goal: Make repeated and overlapping imports safe without dropping legitimate identical purchases.
criteria: Persist immutable import source identity separately from editable transaction fields, including after deletion. Scope source IDs to account and profile/source.
Classify stable source-ID repeats as duplicates and source-ID data conflicts for review. Treat a matching file hash plus mapping as a definite repeat.
Without source IDs, distinguish definite repeats from possible duplicates in overlapping files. Preserve occurrence counts so two identical new $10 purchases remain two purchases.
Include potential manual-record matches in review; never silently skip ambiguous matches. Require explicit keep/skip decisions where appropriate.
Commit all accepted rows, splits, import identities, and batch outcome atomically. Recheck access, identities, and preview freshness at confirmation; stale previews return to review.
Retrying a successful confirmation creates no new rows. Failed confirmation leaves no partial records. An unknown network outcome can be resolved through the stored batch result.
Verify edited/deleted reimports, overlapping exports, identity conflicts, identical rows, simultaneous confirmations, access revocation, stale previews, and rollback.

issues.title: Build CSV import mapping, review, and result screens
issues.goal: Make statement import understandable and prove support for the household's first exports.
criteria: Implement the website-spec stages: file/account, mapping, review, and result, with a visible current step and accessible navigation.
Show new, duplicate, possible-duplicate, conflict, invalid, and excluded counts with row-level explanations.
Let users correct/exclude invalid rows and explicitly keep/skip ambiguous matches. Show confirmation totals before any writes.
Render atomic success/failure results, prevent double submission, and resolve uncertain network outcomes by checking the saved batch before retrying.
Handle changed mappings, stale preview, permission loss, unsupported input, loading, and empty results without misleading success messages.
Demonstrate the agreed anonymized household exports end to end, repeat the same file, and verify the resulting ledger totals. Include actual desktop/phone screenshots.

issues.title: Implement monthly category limits and Budgets screen
issues.goal: Let the household set category limits for each month and see remaining or overspent amounts.
criteria: Store one limit per sheet/category/month in integer minor units. Distinguish an explicit zero limit from an unset limit.
Compute net expense/refund spending across all attribution buckets with the shared calculation. Income and transfers contribute zero.
Compute remaining = limit minus net spending and allow negative values. Display labeled overspending in the specified danger treatment.
Implement monthly editing, persistence, loading/empty/error states, and stale-edit protection. Do not automatically copy prior limits or implement rollover.
Keep unbudgeted categories visible without presenting a fake remaining limit. Archive behavior must preserve historical budgets and reports.
Verify $100 expense minus $20 refund against $150 and $50 limits gives $70 remaining and $30 overspent; later-month refunds affect only that month.
Match the Budgets layout at desktop/phone and preserve keyboard-accessible inline/form editing.

issues.title: Build Overview spending, category budgets, and family attribution
issues.goal: Provide a clear monthly household summary using the same ledger calculations.
criteria: Implement Net spending, Remaining in budgeted categories, and Uncategorized cards; category budget rows; attribution totals; and recent transactions.
Use the selected sheet and month for all sections. Count unbudgeted spending in net spending but exclude it from remaining in budgeted categories.
Use expense/refund splits, include negative net category/attribution values correctly, and exclude income, transfers, and deleted records.
Use the reference fixture as an explicit development/test fixture: net $278.00, budgeted spending $259.50, limits $410.00, remaining $150.50; Ethan $169.50, Parents $90.00, Unassigned $18.50.
Implement first-use, no-limits, empty-month, loading, error, and revoked-access states. Do not add new chart styles or unrelated metrics.
Verify navigation to the ledger/budget actions and actual desktop/phone layout, including the specified 2:1 panel arrangement on desktop.

issues.title: Implement owner invitations, membership transitions, and revocation
issues.goal: Let owners share a sheet only after the invited person accepts.
criteria: Implement owner-only user search/invite/revoke operations. Search by display name and disambiguate every result with username.
Store pending, accepted, declined, and revoked invitation states. Return inviter and sheet identity to invitees without exposing financial records before acceptance.
Accept/decline only as the intended recipient; acceptance atomically creates one non-owner membership and is idempotent under retries and races.
Prevent acceptance of revoked invitations and prevent members from inviting others. Handle duplicate pending/accepted invitations consistently.
Remove membership on owner revocation and enforce loss of access on the next operation, including import confirmation and stale page actions.
Verify unrelated/forged users, owner versus member authority, repeated/concurrent acceptance, declined/revoked states, and cross-sheet isolation.

issues.title: Build invitations and People settings with no-sheet and revoked states
issues.goal: Make sharing visible to owners and invited family members across the application.
criteria: Build owner search results with display name and username, invite feedback, pending/member lists, and revoke/remove confirmation in People settings.
Build global incoming invitations with sheet and inviter identity, accept/decline actions, and a path available even when the invitee has no sheets.
After acceptance, expose the shared sheet through the switcher and open the appropriate welcome/overview state.
Show members the permitted People view without owner-only controls. Admin status does not change this behavior.
On revoked access, clear financial data from the rendered UI/cache and return to a valid sheet or no-sheet state; discard stale selection and block pending actions.
Verify owner/invitee/member flows, empty/loading/error/retry states, keyboard use, and actual desktop/phone screenshots.

issues.title: Add backup scheduling, retention, export, and admin status
issues.goal: Keep the deployed single-process application recoverable without daily manual snapshots.
criteria: Run an in-process daily backup job with startup catch-up; prevent concurrent jobs and make retries safe.
Retain 14 successful daily backups while preserving protected pre-upgrade and pre-restore snapshots.
Expose the specified administrator backup status: last success/failure, next run, and useful recovery guidance. This view reveals no sheet records solely through admin rights.
Provide and document off-host export/rotation commands or host workflow; /backups on the same disk is not the sole recovery copy.
Verify backup during writes, failure reporting, restart catch-up, retention boundaries, protected snapshots, and simultaneous triggers.
Keep browser download/restore and an additional scheduler service outside MVP.

issues.title: Verify money, permissions, concurrency, and responsive MVP flows
issues.goal: Prove that the integrated app meets the agreed behavior and visual handoff spec.
criteria: Run focused automated checks for monetary calculations, sheet isolation, invitation transitions, import identity/retries, stale edits, and atomic rollback.
Drive the real app through manual/split/refund/transfer entry, CSV mapping/review/commit/reimport, month limits, sharing acceptance/revocation, and edit conflicts.
Verify the website-reference fixture totals and the plan's release examples against persisted data, not just reference markup.
Inspect actual app screens at 1440px and 390px; check 320px overflow, keyboard navigation, focus management, accessible labels/statuses, contrast, and 44px touch targets.
Check the relevant empty/loading/error/no-sheet/no-limits/permission-loss/unknown-import-outcome states. Include actual screenshots and reproducible commands/results.
Fix failures in their owning feature before declaring this issue complete. Do not add deferred features as part of the pass.

issues.title: Document deployment and pass Docker persistence and fresh-volume restore
issues.goal: Make the family MVP runnable and recoverable on the selected household host.
criteria: Write concrete fresh-install, environment, migration/upgrade, controlled registration, first-admin, and CLI recovery instructions for the agreed private-network or HTTPS deployment.
Document persistent /data, separate /backups, backup schedule/retention, off-host export, and administrator versus sheet-owner powers.

Run Docker restart/persistence checks and restore a populated snapshot into a fresh volume containing users, memberships, accounts/categories/buckets, transactions/splits, budgets, and import identities.
After restore, require sign-in and prove reimport adds no duplicates. Validate corrupt/incompatible restore rejection and preservation of the prior database.
Record the release checklist, tested image/version, commands, evidence, and known limitations; remove debug/demo data from production startup.
Confirm every MVP tracker item is complete. Keep goals, settlement/debt, balances/reconciliation, bank sync, browser restore, rollover, and multi-currency outside this release.
